name: ProjectSettings
description: Edit notification preferences, then save or discard the draft.
guidance: Use this when changes need an explicit save. Group related fields in one form, keep Save and Discard together, and show validation beside the affected field before applying the draft.

name: CollectionBrowser
description: Search project records, include archived items and open a matching view.
guidance: Use this for a collection that can outgrow a short list. Keep search, filters and the result count together above the list so users can see what changed. Give a filtered empty result a way back to the full collection.

name: DecisionReview
description: Review the observed facts and confirm a revision-bound decision.
guidance: Use this when an action depends on the state a person reviewed. Show the relevant facts beside the decision, then confirm the action against the reviewed revision and report its outcome in place.

name: ConversationPanel
description: Read a thread and send a draft or stop an in-progress reply.
guidance: Use this for an ongoing thread. Place the composer after the transcript, preserve drafts across unrelated updates, and surface Stop beside the composer while a reply is in progress.

name: AgentWorkspace
description: Switch between agents without mixing their conversations, then open the computer inspector as needed.
guidance: Use this when people switch between multiple agents in one session. Keep the agent roster available as they work, scope the transcript and draft to the selected agent, and reveal the runtime inspector on demand.

name: ProjectWorkspace
description: Open a project with its own conversations, sources and instructions.
guidance: Use this when conversations, sources and instructions share a project boundary. Keep the project identity in view and use tabs for peer views so the user can change views without changing projects.

name: OperationsLibrary
description: Browse routines, skills and connections. Inspect and edit an available routine.
guidance: Use this when people browse several types of reusable operations. Give each type a stable tab, put search inside that context, and open editing only after a routine has been selected.

name: AttentionInbox
description: Filter unread work, review an explicit action and read its receipt.
guidance: Use this when people need to distinguish unread updates from work that needs a decision. Keep the unread filter over the list, confirm consequential actions and place their receipts beside the reviewed item.

name: ArtifactLibrary
description: Search artifacts by type, open a preview and pin useful results.
guidance: Use this when people reopen outputs across sessions. Keep type and text filters together, reveal a selected artifact without losing the result list, and show the pinned state on the artifact itself.

name: ProjectAccess
description: Inspect membership, invite someone and review access changes for the selected project.
guidance: Use this when a project has its own members and permissions. Keep invitations separate from editing existing roles and ask for confirmation when a change alters someone else’s access.

name: AgentProfile
description: Edit an agent’s name, silhouette, scope and working instructions.
guidance: Use this when identity and instructions are editable together. Place the live identity preview beside the identity fields and place scope and instructions in a separate group so users can review what each change affects.

name: RunInspector
description: Inspect a routine run, read its result and explicitly request retry or cancel.
guidance: Use this when people need to diagnose or act on one run. Show the current status and result before the trace, and group Retry or Cancel with the run they affect.

name: AgentSidebar
description: Compose a searchable sidebar with agent identities and teams.
guidance: Use this for switching among agents and teams within a workspace. Keep the search at the top, group agents by team and show the selected agent on the entire row.

name: ProjectSidebar
description: Compose nested project views, search and workspace actions.
guidance: Use this when views belong to distinct projects. Nest each view under its project, preserve the active view when a group opens, and keep workspace-wide actions outside the project groups.
